pending.where: Try it yourself, step 7: "If more than two start, press Esc and rerun it: that's a known bug, not your mistake." (line 293)
pending.problem: The round-2 fix didn't hold. In an interactive terminal session, Claude Code starts sub-agents in the background by default, and Esc doesn't stop background sub-agents. A Visitor who sees reviewers multiplying (the case this sentence is for) presses Esc, and the agents keep running and spawning while using up their plan's usage. 'Rerun it' then starts the same fan-out again, in the same cluttered session. The Lesson never gives the key that does stop them.
pending.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, 'Which subagents run in the background': "With nothing configured, a subagent that Claude spawns from your main conversation starts in the background". For interactive terminal sessions, Claude can wait only if fork mode is turned off, and fork mode is "on by default from Claude Code v2.1.302" (the course facts pin Claude Code 2.1.309). The same page says that at a background sub-agent's permission prompt, Esc denies "that one tool call without stopping the subagent". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode: Esc is "Stop the current response or tool call mid-turn". `Ctrl+X Ctrl+K` is the key to "Stop all running background subagents in this session", and you "Press twice within 3 seconds to confirm". The bug itself is at 1.3.1 docs/engineering/code-review.md:59-61.
pending.fix: Replace the step's last sentence with: "If more keep appearing, press Ctrl+X then Ctrl+K, and the same again within 3 seconds, to stop them all: that's a known bug, not your mistake. Then type `/clear` and run it again." (If you also apply the next finding, use the single combined step 7 given there.)

pending.where: Try it yourself, step 7: "Now the real review. Watch for two sub-agents starting together." (line 293); step 8: "Read the report" (line 299); checklist: "It started two sub-agents together, one per axis." (line 304)

quiz.where: Final test spot-same-session, right option d feedback: "It was biased toward its own choices and deep in a full context window. Use `/mattpocock-skills:code-review` from a clean session, so fresh sub-agents do the reviewing." (line 427)
quiz.problem: This feedback gives two wrong reasons, and the round-2 body fix made one of them worse. (1) 'Deep in a full context window' blames a full window, but the course fact and the Context window Lesson both say the dumb zone has nothing to do with how full the window is: an agent gets worse long before the window fills. (2) 'From a clean session, so fresh sub-agents do the reviewing' makes the clean session the reason the sub-agents are fresh. The round-2 body fix now says the opposite: the sub-agents start fresh anyway, and the clean session matters because the agent writing their briefs and passing on their reports shouldn't carry the build. So a reader who gets this question right is taught a reason the body has just corrected.
quiz.evidence: writing-guide.md:76: "The limit is about quality, not window size: current models have 1M-token windows, and a session can be in the dumb zone with most of the window free." content/lessons/02-context-window.md:79: "The line has nothing to do with window size ... a session can slip into the dumb zone with over 80% of its window still free." 02-context-window.md:109: "Quality drops long before the window fills." This Lesson, line 214: "The sub-agents start fresh anyway, but the agent you're talking to writes their briefs and passes on their reports. If it did the building, it brings the build's assumptions." SKILL.md:62-72 and :78: the invoking agent writes both prompts and presents the reports. Line 29 of the body has the same 'is full of the build' framing.
quiz.fix: Line 427: "  > Right. It was biased toward its own choices, and three hours in it was likely past the Smart zone. Use `/mattpocock-skills:code-review` from a clean session, so neither the reviewers nor the agent briefing them built the code."
